l.i: Quas syluæ recreant, umbriferum & nemus, Quas semperiuuat arbores Maturis grauidas cernere fructibus. Ast tu Delphice nunc iube Vt post fata bonas talis ad infulas Ficus carminibus meet Commedata tuis, gratáque manibus Umbras pallidulas ferat, Campis Elysij mollibus infita.

main_text.l: IOANNI BAPTISTÆ ROTHANO AMICO DVLCISSIMO & Ecclesiastæ Geneuensi.

l.i: QVÆ nunc causa, precor, quæve negotia Te Rothane tenent tam procul ædibus Charis? ecquid abes iam nimium diu: Maiorésque trahis pollicito moras?
Tandem, quæso, redi, protinus & fuge Deformata feris Gallica motibus Arua, & purpureas sanguine ciuium Vrbes, & rabidis stragibus horridas.
Coniunx ingenuis orta parentibus, Et cui fida pio pectore castitas

page.notes: The initial Q is a large woodcut letter; the first word is written joined to it. Some words are uncertain in the Latin text of the dedication lines (e.g. "Charis?" and "ædibus"), but read as printed. Running head is "LYRICA." with page number 109.
